maria: Quick follow-up on the progress-pulse idea for long LLM streams. TL;DR: send periodic lightweight progress pulses (small metadata frames) so gateways can checkpoint visible progress and apply bounded retry/backoff without re-synthesizing earlier tokens.
kevin: Interesting. How does this avoid double-emit risk when a retry hits downstream? If we resume, client might see duplicates.
jen: Also, are we adding a lot of state to the gateway? memory concerns at high concurrency.
maria: Good q's. Proposal: pulses are monotonic sequence numbers + server-signed resume token. Gateway persists only the last acked seq + resume token per stream. On retry, gateway uses resume token to request delta from model or from serving runtime; if the resume token is accepted, the upstream will only return new tokens. If not, gateway falls back to hedging/fail-open. This keeps duplicate emission bounded and explicit.
kevin: So upstream/runtime needs to implement a resume API that can accept token+seq? That seems like a new contract.
maria: Yes, small new contract. We only need support for compatible model runtimes. In practice, most dedicated runtimes can support resuming by rewinding KV cache and skipping already-produced tokens.
ryan: What's the operational cost? Does storing resume tokens per stream balloon memory or disk?
maria: We keep a tiny sliding window: only last N pulses and the current resume token. Eviction after inactivity timeout (configurable, default 30s). Memory per stream is O(1) and the token is a small blob (few hundred bytes). We'll add a circuit-breaker when streams > threshold to avoid collapse.
jen: Ok. How do clients opt-in? Backwards compatibility concerns.
maria: Feature-gated. Clients include an opt-in header like `X-Gateway-Pulse: want-resume` and the gateway will emit pulses. If clients don't opt-in, behavior unchanged.
kevin: For transport, gRPC needs inline frames; trailers don't help mid-stream. For HTTP chunked we can piggyback pulse headers in chunk metadata.
ryan: Billing & SLO question: do pulses count as requests or tokens? If we end up resuming a lot, cost could rise.
maria: Pulses are metadata only and do not incur model token billing. Resumes may cause re-generation of delta tokens only; total model tokens billed reflect actual model output. Pulses let us trigger hedging/fast-fail earlier, which should reduce wasted retries overall.
deploy-bot: canary: gateway v2 (pulse-proto) deployed to staging at 2024-09-26T15:10Z :white_check_mark:
kevin: Example minimal pulse frame for HTTP/gRPC:
```
X-Pulse-Seq: 42
X-Resume-Token: abcd1234
X-Pulse-Progress: 512
```
jen: If resume-token verification fails mid-retry we need a clear fallback: either full re-run or hedged branch. Which do we prefer?
maria: Prefer hedged branch + circuit-breaker to prevent thundering restarts. If resume fails frequently, revert to conservative hedging and record telemetry.
kevin: We should also simulate worst-case: client RTT 500ms, model 1s per chunk, high concurrency. Need perf sims to tune N and timeouts.
jen: Agreed. I'll add a memory table and perf sim to the RFC draft.
ryan: Logging/observability: need resume acceptance metrics, resume-fail rates, duplicate-output incidents.
maria: Yep — add counters: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_fail, duplicate_emit_detected. We'll surface per-route.
kevin: One more: how do we protect against malicious resume tokens or replay? Make tokens opaque, signed, TTL-limited.
maria: Token is HMAC-signed by runtime, includes stream-id, seq, and expiry. Gateway verifies signature on resume attempt.
jen: Sounds workable. If this lands, it could reduce tail-latency and make retries less wasteful.
maria: I'll update the RFC with a prototyping plan, perf sim results, and example router changes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
kevin: sgtm
ryan: +1
jen: +1
